// UNITS_S9F_1: librelane declares PL/GRT_RESIZER_*_SLACK_MARGIN as units=ns in its schema, but scripts/openroad/rsz_timing_post{cts,grt}.tcl pass the value RAW to OpenROAD, which reads it in the Liberty time_unit. ASAP7 Liberty (asap7sc7p5t_SEQ_RVT_TT_nldm_220123.lib) is time_unit 1ps -- so these are PS values, NOT ns. The old 0.100/0.150 values meant 0.1-0.15 ps (~0 guard band); every prior ASAP7 sign-off (CPU 1282 MHz, GPU, SoC run 14) ran with effectively zero resizer guard band. Proven by GH #96 runs 17/18: 2.5x change in the (misread) margin produced a byte-identical netlist. See claude_verilog_test-s9f.
// UNITS_S9F_2: Values below are real ps, sized at 2.5% of the 780 ps CPU period for setup / 1.5% for hold, rounded to 5 ps, and kept under the current signed-off slack (+24.011 ps setup / +28.142 ps hold at RUN_2026-06-02_20-37-12) so the guard band cannot demand more than this design is known to achieve. PL and GRT stage margins are set equal (the old 100/150 vs 100/100 stage split was never a deliberate ratio -- both were sub-ps and effectively inert). Re-validate on the next real ASAP7 CPU PD run -- not exercised here.
// PL_RESIZER_TIMING_MAX_PASSES_NOTE: Added 2026-09-19 during the bead ma7 sv2v re-harden: OpenROAD.ResizerTimingPostCTS's repair_timing on the larger (89k-instance-class) sv2v netlist oscillated at ~3240 endpoints / -142..-146 ps WNS for 1650+ Iter within the first pass over 35+ min with no real convergence (same pathology bead bpp already characterized on an earlier, smaller CPU-block test: 'Iter climbed past 2000 within one pass' before concluding -- max_passes alone does not bound the inner per-endpoint retry loop). Fix: this project's own opt-in PL_RESIZER_TIMING_MAX_PASSES hook (rsz_timing_postcts.tcl / rsz_timing_postgrt.tcl, bead bpp, 2026-09-15) forces the outer sweep to stop after N passes so a genuinely-oscillating pass cannot run unbounded. Set to 2 per bpp's recommendation ("start with 1 or 2"). This is an optimizer iteration bound, not an RTL or timing-target change -- it may leave more residual setup violators than an unbounded run would have converged to, which is exactly the tradeoff bpp documents.

// PIN_ORDER_NOTE: FP_PIN_ORDER_CFG pins the macro's boundary pin layout. Without it OpenROAD free-floats pin assignment per block run: two consecutive regenerations moved 393 of 401 pins, which perturbed SoC placement around u_cpu, doubled post-CTS cpu_clk skew (worst_hold -485.6 -> -922.1 ps), drove hold violations 805 -> 4702 endpoints and 4814 inserted hold buffers, and took cpu_clk WNS from -60.66 to -596.00 ps. The file is generated from the known-good run-21 abstract. io_place.py ERRORS if a design pin is missing from the file or vice versa (power/ground are excluded by the tool), so adding a port fails loudly instead of silently reshuffling.
